generation_feedback.diagnosis: S won on measured discovery efficiency, not raw benchmark score. It produced 1 fresh missing pair and 53 fresh pair/seed hits, far exceeding B and D’s 3 hits while preserving their shared 1-pair novelty. This supports combining B’s signature chambers with D’s square-class constraints as a focused engine. C achieved the highest benchmark score (61280.8055) but recorded zero novelty, so its Gaussian-period family mainly reproduced existing coverage. B demonstrated genuine novelty but was pruned after relatively low screen and benchmark scores. D also found the same amount of unique novelty with stronger scores, making it the better backbone. A and E failed through AI-call timeouts; those outcomes say nothing conclusive about their mathematical hypotheses. No discriminant conclusion is possible because every discriminant-improvement field is blank.
generation_feedback.next_generation_direction: Run a fixed-budget ablation of S’s constraint-aware tower engine. On the same small list of biquadratic bases, test three explicitly separated batches: sign-chamber control only, square-class-relation control only, and their joint constraints. Cap each batch at ten expanded octics, deduplicate before expensive verification, impose strict per-polynomial timeouts, and record completion rate, realized signatures, distinct fresh pairs, total fresh hits, seeds, and discriminant results. Retain only joint constraint templates that add distinct novelty rather than repeatedly hitting the already observed pair; keep Gaussian periods to one tiny canary batch and do not enlarge A, C, or E until they pass similarly bounded completion tests.
